Title: Timing question: Heidelburg BEFORE Temptation kicks in? (LSJ?)

Messages.Author: d
Messages.Body:
My prey plays Temptation on one of my vamps, then attempts to take him
immediately and transfer equipment off him.
Can I tap my Heidelberg Castle beforehand? Ie. After the Temptation
action and before the counter burning?

Cheers,

d

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:

Not in the general case. The acting Methuselah gets the first chance.

If the temptation was played via a Madness Network action, perhaps.

That's what I would think.

It may make a difference if you attempt to use Heidelberg during the
Temptation action (before block/before reaction/before "success") vs.
if you attempt to use Heidelberg in response to acting meth declaring
he burns Temptation counters after the action to put Temptation into
play is successful. Former seems fine, latter seems not.

At least, I see these as two discrete "actions" which you can't
"interrupt," but there's a window in there that you can respond to the
initial Temptation within.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:


Yes. With the Meth whose turn it is going first. As her first activity between
actions, she may burn the Temptation counters and take control of the minion.
Then, when she subsequently passes on further effects, you may tap the castle
(but, at this point, you no longer control the Tempted minion, so the castle
can't move stuff to or from him).

Messages.Author: CthuluKitty
Messages.Body:
> Yes. With the Meth whose turn it is going first. As her first activity between
> actions, she may burn the Temptation counters and take control of the minion.
> Then, when she subsequently passes on further effects, you may tap the castle
> (but, at this point, you no longer control the Tempted minion, so the castle
> can't move stuff to or from him).

The only problem about this ruling (or its converse; actually the
whole situation in general) is that you can run afoul of several
slapjack-esque scenarios that could result in arguments and the
possible intervention of a judge. If you had tapped the Castle before
the acting player declared his triggering of Temptation, he might
claim that you had jumped the gun and he wants to do so in his window
of oppurtunity. You might then argue that he is only wanting to
trigger the effect *now* because you tipped your hand, and that a
certain period of silence indicated to you that he was declining to
trigger the Temptation. Luckily, most VTES players are fairly
reasonable people.

In general, the game avoids problems like this by fairly strict timing
rules that govern various sorts of cards. Unfortunately, effects like
Temptation and Heidelberg Castle slip through those cracks because the
"I do something between actions" subphase is not very well defined.

Combat phase timing can be annoying. If we've already established that
my deck will only strike, I will usually say "I strike whatever" and
tell them to play whatever they want whenever appropriate. If, on the
other hand, we have 2 decks with combat thingies to do, I never let
anyone skip the prestrike phase (a quick NO Grapple will suffice), the
Press Step, the end-of-round step (a quick NO Taste), and the after-
combat step (NO Psyche!). It really is just easier to say all these
things every time they're liable to come up than have to argue about
it again and again.


